page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 1890 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in data processing and compression. The single-threaded gzip compression reaches 36.5 GB/sec, placing it in the top tier, while single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs at 15.18 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong at 231.56 GB/sec. The Intel Xeon processor's architecture, which includes AVX-512 and AMX instructions, supports a PassMark CPU score of 54563.93 and a strong encryption test score of 38384.13. Memory bandwidth tests show 2684.62 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 166.74 GB/sec for large uncached blocks.

With its balanced CPU-to-memory ratio and substantial local storage, the D32ds_v7 is well-suited for relational databases, static web serving, and Redis caching operations, where it achieves 61.6 million operations per second. It also handles moderate machine learning tasks, demonstrating strong prompt processing speeds of 219.58 tokens/sec for 7B LLM models, though text generation for larger 70B models is average at 2.81 tokens/sec. The instance offers a balanced resource density, making it a cost-efficient option for enterprise workloads requiring high-speed local storage without the premium cost of memory-optimized hardware.
description: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine from the Ddsv7 family, powered by a 32-vCPU Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 128.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 1890 GB local disk with Premium Storage capabilities. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance delivers strong performance across data processing tasks, with top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 36.5 GB/sec and a PassMark CPU score of 54563.93. It also demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, static web serving at 59.6 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations at 61.6 million operations per second. Lacking a GPU, it is not intended for heavy deep learning training, but it provides cost-efficient, balanced compute and storage resources. This makes it highly suitable for relational databases, enterprise web serving, caching layers, and moderate LLM inference workloads.
